  • We write salient notes on this Zulip. Gotta figure out a good way to have transcript summaries.
  • What calendar? Might wanna use the Lean FRO calendar.
  • We have a general issue of whether we want transition systems and other general patterns to be structures or classes, which spans across languages, automata, and machines. We're currently using structures, and we would like to be consistent. But we also think there's value in exploring the class-based approach (like GraphLike).
  • @Thomas Waring and @Fabrizio Montesi will work on a smaller connective PR.
  • We'll gather agenda points here so that we can prepare for the meeting.
  • We want our algorithms to be run on user-defined data structures, which points to Graph-classes that these algorithms can use.

Following up on the discussion and request in today’s meeting I found one of Bhavik’s DFS samples from 2 years ago. It is not the most general version which I am sure he suggested. But discord search is not good at finding stuff like this from two years ago.

I am not sure it would even compile today given that almost 20 toolchains have been released since then. But I think we can make it simpler with recent toolchains.

@Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai

One of Bhavik's DFS examples

variable {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]

def SimpleGraph.neighborList (v : Fin n) : List (Fin n) := (List.finRange n).filter (G.Adj v)

def dfs_stack_list : List (Fin n) → List (Fin n) → List (Fin n)
  | visited, [] => visited
  | visited, x :: xs =>
      if h : x ∈ visited
        then dfs_stack_list visited xs
        else
          have : (visited.toFinsetᶜ.erase x).card < _ := Finset.card_erase_lt_of_mem (by simpa)
          dfs_stack_list (x :: visited) (G.neighborList x ++ xs)
  termination_by v l => (v.toFinsetᶜ.card, l.length)

def dfs (start : Fin n) : List (Fin n) := dfs_stack_list G [] [start]

Here's a version in an old commit of DGAlgorithms based on this :
Very old and now deleted example. Note that the SimpleFingraph here can be trivially replaced by SimpleGraph and using SimpleGraph.neighborFinset
Was the meeting recorded?
I also hope the meeting is recorded. The current meeting time is not convenient for me (US west coast).

No, but we have notes (special thanks to @Alexandre Rademaker for drafting!):

  1. We've discussed how to respond faster when PR authors deal with comments. Sometimes reviewers don't notice that their comments have been dealt with, and PRs linger. We agreed to create a dedicated CSLib: Pull Requests channel (or something with a similar name) where each topic focuses entirely on a single PR and its status, and discussing things that do not pertain getting the PR accepted is gonna be out of scope.
  2. What about abandoned PRs? Perhaps we can use the same channel in point (1) to discuss closing them. A notification bot could also be useful.
  3. We've discussed how to go forward with the graph data structures, and had a long technical discussion about those and the current plans in mathlib. At the end of the discussion we agreed that there's value in going ahead with cslib#503 while we wait for mathlib to progress in this area, since this is blocking a growing list of work to be PRed that provides good context on ergonomics and utility (which might also be interesting for mathlib itself). @Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai will keep tabs on relevant progress and possible linkups with how things are gonna be done in mathlib (especially GraphLike). We also agreed to have another round for making some names in cslib#503 clearer and to pursue a structured hierarchy of these concepts in the near future.
  4. See #CSLib > Copyright header change proposal.
  5. @Thomas Waring and I are working on typeclasses for logical operators in https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/tree/fmontesi/connectives. There's good progress.
  6. I'm dealing with a long bugfix in LTS regarding saturated multistep transitions, which I'm prioritising because the current EpsilonNA acceptance criterion is wrong.
  7. @Shreyas Srinivas wants to add GameTheory to CSLib and I thought it's a good idea (I can imagine multiple places that would benefit from game theory).

Edited to add point 7 (thanks @Nadim Farhat).
I still hope the meetings can be recorded. Lots of nuances are lost in a textual summary.
